standard_prerequisites.name: Cardinal inequality
standard_prerequisites.statement: alpha<=beta means there is an injection from a representative of alpha to a representative of beta.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the relation whose preorder laws are asserted.

standard_prerequisites.name: Truncation induction on card
standard_prerequisites.statement: card is the 0-truncation of the type of sets, so a mere proposition indexed by card may be proved by assuming the index is cd{A}.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is what lets the proof pass from cardinals to sets.

standard_prerequisites.name: Induction on propositional truncation
standard_prerequisites.statement: To prove a mere proposition from a propositional truncation it suffices to assume a witness.
standard_prerequisites.use: It extracts the injections from the truncated inequalities.

core_obligations: Prove transitivity: since the goal is a mere proposition, use induction on the 0-truncation to take alpha, beta, gamma to be cd{A}, cd{B}, cd{C}, and then induction on the propositional truncation to obtain injections f:A->B and g:B->C (source lines 797-798).
Conclude cd{A}<=cd{C} from the composite injection g∘f (source line 799).
Prove reflexivity, which the author records as immediate from the identity injection (source line 800).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce the mere proposition twice by truncation induction, first on card and then on the truncation inside the inequality.
Compose the two injections and read off transitivity.
Record reflexivity from the identity injection.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the unlabelled lemma at source lines 787-794, original Lemma 10.2.8: for cardinal numbers alpha, beta, gamma one has alpha<=alpha and (alpha<=beta)->(beta<=gamma)->(alpha<=gamma). It has no author label, so its first-edition number is part of its identity. The proof (source lines 795-801) is short but proceeds by two nested truncation eliminations: the outer one replaces the three cardinals by sets, the inner one extracts the two injections from the truncated inequalities, and the author states at once that both uses are legitimate because the goal is a mere proposition. The statement records the two preorder laws and neither reduction; the author disposes of reflexivity with the remark that it is even easier, the identity injection being the evident witness.
